ticket.title: Make miter verify the documented Tier 1 loop, since cargo check cannot finish inside an agent tool window
ticket.description:
Observed 2026-11-06 across roughly twenty build invocations: every 'cargo check --workspace --all-targets' exceeded the 30s tool window and had to be backgrounded and polled, burning two or three turns per build. Tier 1 in AGENTS.md prescribes cargo check -p <crate>; miter verify already exists for exactly this shape of problem and returns sliced diagnostics with zero build scrollback. Worth doing: measure miter verify cold and warm against cargo check on a real crate, and if it wins, rewrite Tier 1 in AGENTS.md to name it, with cargo as the fallback. It also sidesteps the shared build-lock stall in GB-236 better than polling a log.

SCOPE CLARIFIED 2026-11-06 (owner): storypole verify --compiler already shells out to `miter verify` (storypole-core/src/ops/verification/mod.rs:48 via run_miter_verify), so miter verify IS already trusted for the closing gate and the receipt records the diagnostic count. That does not cover Tier 1, which is the inner loop DURING development: storypole verify needs a task that is InProgress and resolves its target from the ticket scope, so it cannot answer "did my last edit compile" mid-change. The gap is exactly two things - the documented inner-loop command, and speed. Measure `miter verify --path <crate> --json` cold and warm against `cargo check -p <crate>`; if it wins, Tier 1 in AGENTS.md should name it with cargo as the fallback.
